title: The Bestiary
tagline: look things up by name, not by searching
hints: `#include <map>`, then `std::map<std::string, int> hoard;`. Counting is the one place `hoard[name]++` is exactly right - a missing key is created as 0 first, which is what you want here.

Iterating: `for (const auto& entry : hoard)` gives you pairs. `entry.first` is the key, `entry.second` is the value. C++17 lets you write `for (const auto& [name, count] : hoard)` instead, which reads far better.
A std::map is always sorted by key, so the alphabetical order is free - do not sort anything yourself.

For the LOOKUP use `find`: `auto it = hoard.find("gold coin");` then `if (it == hoard.end())` means not present. Using `hoard["gold coin"]` here would silently INSERT it and change your distinct count.
`distinct` is `hoard.size()`. `total` is the sum of every `.second`.
